title: GPU nodegroup staged rollout with drift detection and health probes - terraform module
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a reusable Terraform module for Private (VPC) deployments to manage GPU nodegroups with an opinionated staged rollout path that supports both ASG and Karpenter-backed pools. The module will include automated drift detection, cross-AZ health probes, safe node draining hooks, and a canary/preview rollout strategy. This is intended to reduce upgrade blast radius, make upgrades observable, and unify our private IaC patterns for GPU fleets.
background: We currently have multiple bespoke terraform configurations across clusters for GPU pools and different autoscalers. Upgrades and driver changes have resulted in post-upgrade capacity loss and lengthy remediation. There is no standard drift detection for GPU AMI/kernel mismatch or node-taint/label divergence. Karpenter and ASG variants require slightly different lifecycle handling; we need a single module that expresses the common contract and provides extendable lifecycle hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module 'redwood_gpu_pool' exists with clear variables to select mode: 'asg' or 'karpenter'
Module exposes lifecycle hooks: pre_update_lambda, post_update_hook (SNS/webhook) and an optional operator job for canary verification
Staged rollout plan: canary pool (1-2 nodes) -> 10% rollout -> 50% rollout -> full. Each stage must be stoppable and auto-rollback on health failure
Drift detection: scheduled plan that compares live node labels/taints/AMI/driver version against module configuration and writes findings to S3 + alert to infra-alerting channel
Health probes: node-level GPU healthcheck (nvidia-smi smoke), kubelet readiness probe thresholds, and integration with cluster-autoscaler/karpenter to avoid premature scale-down during upgrades
Upgrade runbook is included in module docs and validated by automated integration test in staging
Module has unit tests (terraform validate + fmt) and an end-to-end terratest or CI pipeline that performs a staged upgrade in a non-prod VPC and asserts no disruption to running inference workloads
tasks: Draft module API and variables; review with infra and platform teams
Implement core resources for ASG variant (launch template, autoscaling group, IAM roles, lifecycle hooks)
Implement Karpenter variant (provisioner templates, NodePool CRD mapping, taints/labels management)
Add optional lambda that performs node health probe and GPU driver smoke test during lifecycle
Implement drift detection job (scheduled terraform plan + comparator) and S3 report + alerting
Build staged-rollout controller (small operator or workflow in GH Actions) to orchestrate stages and stop/rollback on failed checks
Write docs, runbook, and migration steps for existing clusters
Add CI integration tests and staging validation; run two dry-run upgrades in staging cluster
implementation_plan: Week 1: Design API, align on common labels/taints and kubelet configuration defaults
Week 2: ASG implementation + LB-friendly lifecycle hooks and pre/post scripts
Week 3: Karpenter implementation + mapping layer to reuse ASG lifecycle tests
Week 4: Drift detection + scheduled report; integrate with PagerDuty/Slack alerting
Week 5: Staged-rollout controller + canary verification jobs
Week 6: Docs, runbook, CI tests, and staging upgrades
Post-merge: Gradual adoption plan and one live cluster migration with on-call present
migration_steps: Identify current GPU pools and their autoscaler type via inventory script (link to runbook)
Create feature-flagged namespace and provision module's canary pool into staging-like partition
Run small inference traffic against canary and validate metrics (latency, error-rate, GPU temp)
Execute staged rollout with automated verification; if verification fails, rollback via terraform apply with previous module variables
Once validated, update production clusters during maintenance window with on-call and rollback triggers enabled
test_plan: Unit: terraform fmt/validate and module variable edge-case matrix
Integration: terratest scenario that provisions a small VPC cluster, provisions GPU pool (ASG and Karpenter) and runs node drain/update
Chaos: simulate kubelet restart and GPU driver crash to validate health probes and rollback
Observability: ensure metrics emitted (upgrade_stage, canary_result, drift_finds) and dashboards created
Pre-merge: PR must include passing CI and a staging run summary document
notes: Prefer immutable launch template/AMI upgrade pattern to reduce time drifting between nodes
Consider pinning NVIDIA driver versions via package manifest and integrate with our optimize pipeline
Work with security for IAM role scoping for lifecycle lambdas and S3 reports
Ensure VPC endpoints or NAT egress exists for nodes that need to download drivers during boot in private deployments
